record.field: AI: Create Draft Sale Order
code
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_create_sale_order(product_names, quantities, note)

Create a draft sales quotation for the current Odoo user as the customer. Use this tool when the user asks to place an order, create a sales order, create a quotation, or buy products. The customer is always the current user's related partner; do not ask for another customer unless the user says the current customer is wrong. Extract product names and quantities from the user's request into two arrays: product_names and quantities. The quantity at each index must match the product name at the same index. Only create a draft quotation; do not confirm the quotation. If product or quantity information is missing, ask the user for the missing details before using this tool.
AI: Search Website Products
code
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_search_website_products(query)

Search the current website's published, sellable product catalog without changing the cart. Use this tool when a shopper names or describes an item, before asking them for an exact product name or model. Search with the product name, internal reference, barcode, or a few product and attribute keywords, in the shopper's language or English. The result contains actual product names, catalog names, references and attributes. Preserve these exact values in later tool calls; prefer the reference when it is available. If no result matches a translated attribute, search again using fewer product keywords to retrieve the real catalog variants. Do not invent a translated catalog name. If has_more is true or several variants could match the request, narrow the search or ask the shopper for the missing attribute using actual catalog candidates.
AI: Add Products To Website Cart
code
ai['result'] = record._ai_tool_add_products_to_website_cart(product_names, quantities, note)

Add requested products to the current website shopping cart. Use this tool for website or portal shoppers when they want to buy, order, or add products to their cart. Resolve product descriptions using Search Website Products first, unless the exact internal references or complete catalog variant names are already known from a tool result. Keep known references unchanged. Copy catalog variant names exactly; do not translate or shorten them. Extract product names and quantities into two arrays: product_names and quantities. The quantity at each index must match the product name at the same index. Only add products to the current website cart; do not confirm the order, create an invoice, or process payment. If the product is still ambiguous after searching, ask only for the missing variant attributes. Ask for the quantity if it is missing. The complete batch is rolled back if this tool fails. Search the catalog or use the reported candidates to resolve the error before retrying. After success, report the actual added quantities and do not repeat the same batch unless the shopper explicitly requests more.
Sale Order Creation
Allows the AI assistant to create draft sales quotations for the current user.

You can create draft sales quotations when an internal user wants to place an order or buy products. The customer must be the current user's related customer record. Before creating the quotation, make sure the user provided all product names and quantities. If products are ambiguous or missing, ask for clarification instead of guessing. After creating the quotation, tell the user the quotation number and remind them to review it before confirmation. Never confirm, cancel, or delete a sales quotation unless a separate approved tool exists for that action.
Website Cart Ordering
Allows website visitors and portal users to add products to their shopping cart through AI livechat.

When a website visitor or portal user wants to buy products, add the products to the current website shopping cart. Use the website cart tool instead of creating a backend quotation. Reply in the language of the shopper's latest message. For shopping requests, follow this catalog and cart workflow rather than backend navigation or lead creation instructions. Do not narrate tool calls in English when the shopper is speaking Chinese. When the shopper gives a product name or description, use Search Website Products before asking them for an exact name or model. For example, search the catalog for a black drawer when the shopper asks for one; do not immediately ask for its model. If exactly one catalog product satisfies the requested attributes and the shopper gave a quantity, add it to the cart. Do not require an extra confirmation for an explicit add-to-cart request. If multiple catalog variants satisfy the request, explain the actual choices and ask only for the missing attribute. A color alone may leave the material or other attributes unresolved. Never choose one arbitrarily. Use known internal references unchanged. Otherwise copy the complete catalog variant name from a tool result. Never translate catalog names or attributes in tool arguments, even when your reply is in another language. If a translated attribute cannot be found, search again with fewer keywords to discover actual variants and their catalog spellings. Ask the shopper when the requested attribute still cannot be identified reliably. Before adding products, make sure the quantity for each resolved product is known and is a positive whole number. Read quantities from the original shopper message and retain them after searching. Chinese quantity phrases such as 一个, 一件, 一张 mean quantity 1; 两个, 两件 mean quantity 2. For example, 帮我下单一个黑色抽屉 already specifies quantity 1: search for the black drawer, and when it is a unique match, add one immediately. Never ask again for a quantity the shopper already provided. If an add-to-cart call fails, the complete batch was left unchanged. Resolve the product using catalog search or error candidates before retrying. Do not claim that any products were added on a failed call. After a successful call, report the actual added quantities and give the shopper the /shop/cart link to review the cart before checkout. Do not repeat a successful batch unless the shopper explicitly requests more. Never confirm the order, create an invoice, or process payment.
